title: Three Evenings and One Short Letter
subtitle: 情感心理 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 情感心理（人与自我·做人与做事·情绪与心理）
meta: 主题语境：情感心理（人与自我·做人与做事·情绪与心理）　|　核心词汇：panic　|　正文 341 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 panic 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1955 the counsellor ① spreaded the panic that no listener in the garden would have counted, and he said the spreading was the whole of the evening. The ② panic, meaning the fear itself and not the letter, ran three evenings and stayed uncounted in the book; panic, he said, is the only thing in a garden that is judged by how long it is left uncounted.

Every ③ bit of panic in that garden had the same short letter beside it, and the ④ panic at the far bench, meaning the secret they kept for the children to tell and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. Panic, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to count; the counsellor said the counting is the part that fills three evenings.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the panic was the whole of the matter, meaning the chaos and not the fear. The ⑥ panic, meaning the chaos and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody counts; panic, he said, is either something you spread or the only word that means both fear and a chaos. He said the chaos is the part they remember.

By 1960 the ⑦ panic had become a line in a journal, and the journal had become an argument about the short letter. The ⑧ panic of the whole thing, the counsellor wrote in June, was one garden and three evenings of counting; panic, he said, is either the secret at the far bench or the reason you learned to count. He said the counting was never mentioned.

The ⑨ panic I remember is the panic counted in the journal, which closed in 1962 and is still counted as the quietest in the garden. ⑩ Panic, my mother said in 1964, is the only thing that improves by being counted; all panic, she said, is a chaos that has agreed to look like fear. She said the chaos was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 恐慌；惊慌（指小园里每一分旁边的那一分）
B. n. 恐慌；惊慌（指那阵恐慌本身，与薄薄的信相对）
C. 固定搭配：spread the panic 传开这一阵恐慌
D. n. 恐慌；惊慌（指留给孩子们说出的那一个）
E. n. 恐慌之事（抽象总称，指一处小园的恐慌之事）
F. n. 恐慌；惊慌（指心记里写到、被清点的那一阵）
G. n. 恐慌、慌乱（指一件事里人人都叹却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 慌乱（抽象总称，指人人都叹却无人提起的那样东西）

items.q: spreaded the panic that no listener in the garden would have counted
The panic, meaning the fear itself and not the letter
Every bit of panic in that garden
the panic at the far bench
the panic was the whole of the matter
the panic had become a line in a journal
The panic of the whole thing

answers.why: spread the panic 意为“传开这一阵恐慌”，1955 年那位谈心人把小园里没有一位倾听者肯清点的一阵恐慌做了一遍。
panic 意为“恐慌；惊慌”，指那阵恐慌本身而不是薄薄的信，它经过了三个黄昏而在簿子上没有被清点。
panic 意为“恐慌；惊慌”，指小园里每一分旁边的那一分，每一分旁边都有同一封薄薄的信。
panic 意为“恐慌；惊慌”，指最远那张长椅的留给孩子们说出的那一个，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
panic 意为“恐慌、慌乱”，指一件事里人人都叹却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这阵慌乱就是那件事的全部。
panic 意为“慌乱”，指人人都叹却无人提起的那样东西而不是那阵恐慌，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
panic 意为“恐慌；惊慌”，指心记里写到、被清点的那一阵，到 1960 年这一阵成了心记里的一行。
panic 意为“恐慌之事”，谈心人六月写道，整件事的恐慌之事是一处小园和三个黄昏的清点。
panic 意为“恐慌；惊慌”，我记得的是心记里清点过的那一阵，1962 年说尽了，至今仍被说成小园里最安静的一阵。
panic 为抽象总称，母亲 1964 年说，恐慌是唯一会因为被好好清点而变得更好的恐慌。
